note: Carried launchers found in installed game content with no catalogue entry (tools/report_match_coverage.py, carried-launcher gap list). A launcher fires a rocket or a recoilless round, so it has no rifling and none is recorded; what it does have is a published mass, which is what the carried load needs. Where the maker publishes an empty and a loaded mass, the entry takes the EMPTY one for a reloadable launcher, whose round is carried as ammunition, and the LOADED one for a disposable launcher, which is issued as one item and cannot be reloaded.

weapons.name: RPG-29 Vampir
weapons.source_note: English Wikipedia 'RPG-29', infobox Mass: '12.1 kg (27 lb) unloaded (with optical sight) / 18.8 kg (41 lb) loaded (ready to fire)'. The UNLOADED mass is taken, because the corpus's weapon mass is the weapon's own and the round is carried as ammunition. A rocket launcher has no rifled barrel, so no twist is recorded.

weapons.name: M3 MAAWS (Carl Gustaf M3)
weapons.source_note: English Wikipedia 'Carl Gustaf 8.4 cm recoilless rifle', infobox Mass: 'M2: 14.2 kg / M3: 10 kg / M4+M3A1: 6.6 kg'; body: 'In US military service, it is officially known as the M3 Multi-Role Anti-Armor Anti-Personnel Weapon System (MAAWS) or Ranger Antitank Weapons System (RAWS), but is often simply called the M3 Carl Gustaf'. The M3 mass is taken, because M3 MAAWS is the M3. The barrel IS rifled, but the corpus holds the rifling twist for a cartridge-firing small arm and this article states none, so no twist is recorded.

The AT4 mass is taken for the M136, which the article states is the American AT4. A rocket launcher has no rifled barrel, so no twist is recorded.
